source_title: New Indian sanctuary | SPACES by Welspun Living - India Today
source_excerpt: The bedroom is undergoing a profound evolution. No longer just a place to sleep, it has transformed into a personal sanctuary—a space to disconnect, reclaim privacy and escape constant information overload. Consumer research by SPACES by Welspun Living across four Indian metros reveals that today’s consumers want their bedrooms to do less and more: less clutter, but more calm, comfort, and personal expression.Responding to this shift, the SPACES Autumn-Winter 2026 (AW26) collection rejects a single vision of the perfect bedroom. Leadership in the home category is not about following trends. It’s about understanding the consumer’s unspoken need and answering it before they realize they’ve been waiting for it,” says Dipali Goenka, managing director and CEO of Welspun Living,This philosophy shapes the collection’s focus on longevity. While consumers shop with their eyes, they sleep with their skin. True premium quality is now measured by how a product feels at midnight. A prime example is the Revive Sleep System, featuring innovative HygroCotton technology, which allows bedding to actually become softer through repeated washing.Jayanti Ganguly, CEO of Home Centre India, sees a consumer increasingly unwilling to accept a single definition of premium. What homeowners choose is deeply personal. As the visual vocabulary of the Indian consumer expands, material matters as much as appearance. While the eye attracts, the hand convinces, and the body decides.This experiential approach extends seamlessly to the SPACES Gifting Studio, which curates premium sheets, quilts and bath combinations across price tiers. Ultimately, the emerging luxury in Indian homes is neither minimalism nor maximalism—it is authorship. The future of home is no longer about creating spaces we want to be seen in, but creating spaces we want to come back to.- Ends
